In view of my due discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.22,57,000/ (Rupees twenty two lakhs fifty seven thousand only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount with interest @ 6% P.A. from the date of petition till the date of deposit to the petitioners within two months from the date of this order.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the petitioners together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled the share of 60%.
And the petitioner No.2 is entitled the share of 30% and the petitioner No.3 is entitled for share of 10%, out of the total award amount.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 & 2, shall deposit 40% out of their share, in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice, for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to them through due process of law.

opennyai_summary.issue:
On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, for final determination of this case, my predecessor in office had framed the following issues:
 *ISSUES*
 1) Whether the petitioners prove  that, Shri Chennaiah, had died due to  the injuries sustained by him in a  motor vehicle accident that was  taken place on 3.3.3022 at about  1.50 p.m. on Magadi H.Durga road,
 7 SCCH-18 MVC 2202/2022  near Byranahalli gate, Kasaba Hobli,
 Magadi Taluk, Ramanagara District  due to the rash and negligent driving  of the driver of the KSRTC bus  bearing registration NO.KA42F1711  in an actionable negligence?
 2) Whether the petitioners are  entitled for compensation as prayed  for?
If so, at what rate?
From whom?
3) What order or award?
opennyai_summary.facts: Consequently, husband of the petitioner No.1, father of the petitioner No.2 and son of the petitioner No.3  9 SCCH-18 MVC 2202/2022 by name Shri Chennaiah. had died.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
13. On the other hand, the respondent, though not denied the accident, and the death of Chennaiah,
seriously disputed the allegation of the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle stating that, there was a sole negligence of the deceased, to cause accident.
And as on the date of the accident, the deceased had no valid driving licence to ride the vehicle.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On the basis of her first information,
criminal law set in motion against the driver of the  11 SCCH-18 MVC 2202/2022 offending vehicle alleging that, he had committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 304(A)
of IPC.
If at all, the driver of the offending vehicle was innocent, and if at all there was a contributory negligence, what prevented to the driver of the offending vehicle to give counter complaint in this regard.
Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.
Since in the death case, the legal heirs are the claimants.
On the other hand, the respondent herein, has not produced documents on record, to show the independent economic status of the petitioners.
And to disprove their dependency,
with the deceased during his life time.
On going through same, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 1.1.1979.
The accident occurred on 3.3.2022.
Hence I am of the view that, as on the date of the accident deceased was aged about 43 years.
To show that, the deceased was earning Rs.4,00,000 per annum from agriculture,
sericulture and by doing milk vending business, no satisfactory documentary evidence is available on record for consideration.
And in support of Ex.P10 to Ex.P12, no evidence of supportive witnesses are available on record.
In such a situation, as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
Hence, the income of the deceased is apt to be taken as Rs.15,500/ p.m., which will meet the ends of justice.

15  26.
Having considered the above as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3rd) where the number of  21 SCCH-18 MVC 2202/2022 dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependant family members exceeds six."
In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
In the present case, deceased was aged about 43 years, as on the date of the accident.
And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
opennyai_summary.decision:
As such by taking into consideration of the selfemployment mentioned in the petition, I am of the view that, 25%
income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects. Therefore, by considering Smt.Bhagyamma vs The Managing Director on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57639599/
16  22 SCCH-18 MVC 2202/2022 the earning of the deceased as Rs.15,500/ per month.
And Rs.1,86,000/ per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 25% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.1,86,000+46,500) =
Rs.2,32,500/.
And 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
Which comes to Rs.21,70,000/.
 27.
The aforesaid amount  should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every  three years.
28 . In the light of the proposition laid down in the aforesaid case, I am of the view that, In addition to this the petitioner No.1 being the wife of the deceased, the petitioner No.2 being the daughter of the deceased and the petitioner No.3 being the mother of the deceased, are entitled for sum of Rs.40,000/ in the head of loss of consortium.
Further, the petitioners are also entitled for sum of Rs.15,000/ towards funeral expenses.
And also the  24 SCCH-18 MVC 2202/2022 petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.15,000/ in the head of loss to the estate.
Further the petitioners are entitled for Rs.10,000/ towards transportation of dead body.
Apart from this, it is to be noted that, in Pranay Sethi's case, the Honourable Apex court,
observed that, after expiry of every three years, from the date of judgment, 10% is to be added to Rs.70,000/ towards conventional heads.
Which comes to Rs.7,000/ Hence, the claimants are entitled for Rs.77,000/ towards conventional Smt.Bhagyamma vs The Managing Director on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57639599/
18 heads.
 29.
Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation under the following heads.
Compensation heads Compensation  Amount  Towards loss of Rs.21,70,00000
dependency  Towards loss of Rs. 44,00000  consortium
25 SCCH-18 MVC 2202/2022  Towards loss of estate Rs. 16,50000  Towards funeral & Rs. 16,50000  obsequies ceremony  expenses  Towards transportation of Rs. 10,00000  dead body  Total Rs.22,57,00000  30.
Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.22,57,000/
(Rupees twenty two lakhs fifty seven thousand only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in MFA No.
103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated.
20.03.2018.
As such, the respondent being the owner cum internal insurance company,
has to pay compensation to the petitioner, with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
ISSUE NO.3:
 32.
In view of my due discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.22,57,000/ (Rupees twenty two lakhs fifty seven thousand only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount with interest @ 6% P.A. from the date of petition till the date of deposit to the petitioners within two months from the date of this order.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the petitioners together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled the share of 60%.
And the petitioner No.2 is entitled the share of 30% and the petitioner No.3 is entitled for share of 10%, out of the total award amount.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 & 2, shall deposit 40% out of their share, in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice, for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to them through due process of law.
20 With regard to the quantum of compensation of petitioner No.3, since the award amount is very meagre, entire amount shall be released to her through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/ .
